prompt: Model undo/redo with two ArrayDeque stacks, where applying a fresh action discards the redo history. Complete the five methods, then run the tests.
explanation: Undo/redo is the textbook two-stack problem: undo pops from done and pushes onto undone, and redo does exactly the reverse, so each method is four lines plus an emptiness guard. Clearing undone inside apply is what models branching history -- once you do something new, the future you had undone is no longer reachable. ArrayDeque.push adds at the head, so iterating done runs newest-to-oldest and currentState has to reverse a copy.
hints: push/pop on an ArrayDeque both work at the head, which is exactly stack behaviour.
undo and redo are mirror images: check isEmpty first and return null, otherwise pop from one stack and push onto the other.
Iterating an ArrayDeque that you pushed onto goes newest first, so currentState can copy it into an ArrayList and call Collections.reverse.
